newsitem.title: USA: Clinton hails Pathfinder space probe landing.
newsitem.headline: Clinton hails Pathfinder space probe landing.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Friday hailed the landing of the Pathfinder space probe on Mars as a remarkable feat and a testament to the ingenuity of Americans.
"Our return to Mars today marks the beginning of a new era in the nation's space exploration programme," Clinton said in a written statement.

Noting that the Mars Pathfinder was the first of a series of probes the United States would send to the planet over the next decade, Clinton said the information they gathered would "help us better undertand our own world and perhaps provide further clues on the origins of our solar system."

"I congratulate the Mars Pathfinder team at NASA and the Jet Propulsion Laboratory for their pioneering vision and spirit in accomplishing this remarkable feat. Their success ... is a testament to the ingenuity and 'can do' attitude of the American people," he said.

Clinton added that the mission underscored the new streamlined and businesslike attitude at the National Aeronautics and Space Administration, pointing out that it was accomplished in one-third the time and at a fraction of the cost of the first Viking mission to Mars.

"On this important day, the American people celebrate another exciting milestone in our nation's long heritage of progress, discovery and exploration -- the first landing on the surface of Mars in over 20 years," the president said.
